purpose: Targeted out-of-sample discrimination of the frozen 31-feature tail-value model against the simpler frozen v1 gap<=11 continuation rule. Ordinary random holdout produced identical decisions, so this experiment screens only pre-outcome index65 states and reveals future outcomes exclusively for disagreement cases.
frozen_v1_decision_at65: Continue iff a positive certificate already exists OR challenger is unresolved and best_gap65<=11; otherwise stop. This experiment compares only unresolved no-certificate index65 decisions.
screening: For every pool case, compute the retained two-arm incumbent and exactly the first 65 seeded-challenger compilations only. Do not evaluate any candidate after index65 before disagreement status is persisted. Record frozen model probability/prediction and v1 gap decision. Cases exhausted/certified before65 are excluded from disagreement analysis because both policies have a deterministic action.
outcome_reveal: After the complete 160-case screening table and disagreement list are durably persisted, finish the full seeded challenger only for every disagreement case. Do not reveal tail outcomes for agreement cases in this experiment.

primary_comparison.label: whether full tail eventually produces any verified endpoint below incumbent
primary_comparison.quality_difference: Sum eventual live-node gain that model would recover minus gain v1 would recover across disagreements.
primary_comparison.tail_compute_difference: Sum post-index65 challenger compilations purchased by model minus those purchased by v1 across disagreements, assuming a continuing policy finishes the challenger; shared prefix cost cancels.

reports: screening counts and disagreement prevalence by family
future-positive rate and gain distribution separately for model-only and v1-only disagreements
model-minus-v1 recovered live-node gain and extra tail candidate compilations
every false negative with seed, gap65, model p, certificate index and gain
no scalar utility or threshold retuning on this pool
scope: Synthetic positive-monotone graph 2-CNF ROBDD ordering. This is a targeted policy-disagreement test, not an unbiased estimate of overall solver success.
